takeaway: Compute-optimal pre-training, RLVR post-training, and log-linear inference-time scaling compound smoothly while preserving >=96% retrieval to 1M context.
caption: Synthetic frontier-model release telemetry (NeurIPS full width, 139.7 mm). (a) Pre-training validation loss across five parameter scales (1B–400B) and the compute-optimal power-law frontier. (b) Reinforcement learning post-training trajectories (mean ± 1 SD across 5 seeds) on AIME '25, GPQA Diamond, and SWE-bench. (c) Test-time compute scaling with thinking-token budget versus no-thinking baseline. (d) Long-context needle retrieval recall from 4k to 1M tokens across document depth. All data are synthetic.
label: fig:frontier_scaling

panels.note: Five model scales (1B–400B) trace a power-law Pareto envelope with alpha = 0.054 above L_inf = 1.24 nats.
RLVR post-training lifts AIME '25 from 38% to 88%, GPQA to 82%, and SWE-bench to 77% over 40k steps.
Scaling thinking tokens from 256 to 64k adds +35 pts on Frontier-400B, outperforming Prior Gen at every budget.
Single-needle recall stays 99–100% through 512k tokens and 96–99% across depths at 1M context.
